metric_definitions.frac_primary: primary_cell_count / cell_count - the share of cells in the dataset that were generated by that study itself
metric_definitions.library_reused_cell_share: library-wide 1 - sum(primary)/sum(cells): the share of cells that are not primary to their own dataset, i.e. reused from another study
metric_definitions.control_reuse_frac: share of control-arm cells in the collection that are not primary to their own dataset (control labels = normal / healthy / control and similar)
metric_definitions.case_reuse_frac: the same ratio for the case arm of the collection; reported alongside so that ordinary atlas aggregation is not mistaken for control-arm contamination
metric_definitions.reuse_asymmetry: control_reuse_frac - case_reuse_frac; only values above 0 mean the control arm depends on externally sourced cells more than the case arm does
metric_definitions.depth_ratio: cell-weighted mean_genes_per_cell, control arm / case arm; computed only from datasets with frac_primary ~ 1
metric_definitions.arm_class: datasets classified by disease label: ctl_only (control labels only) / dis_only (disease labels only) / mixed (control and disease labels inside the same dataset). A mixed dataset carries its contrast internally and its arms cannot be separated at the metadata layer, so it is counted separately rather than folded into the case arm.
metric_definitions.has_arm_contrast: the collection has both ctl_only and dis_only datasets, so the control and case arms can be audited separately
metric_definitions.has_mixed_contrast: the collection contains at least one mixed dataset: a contrast exists but its arms are not separable
metric_definitions.n_any_contrast_collections: number of collections with has_arm_contrast or has_mixed_contrast
metric_definitions.share_contrast_collections_not_arm_separ: among contrast-bearing collections, the share whose arms cannot be separated at the metadata layer
metric_definitions.share_contrast_bearing_ds_fully_reused: share of mixed datasets with frac_primary = 0 (fully reused)

caveat: is_primary_data=False is not itself an error: atlas-style collections legitimately aggregate external data. The conclusions of this audit rest on the **asymmetry** (the control arm depending on externally sourced cells more than the case arm does) and on the share of **fully reused control arms**, not on the absolute reuse rate. mean_genes_per_cell is a dataset-level mean and serves only as a depth proxy. The most important limitation of this audit is that audit feasibility is itself filtered by data quality: of the 140 contrast-bearing collections in the library only 10.7% have arms that can be separated at the metadata layer, and in those 15 auditable collections the control arm is almost always primary to its own study - that is, the auditable subset happens to be the clean-control subset. For 89.3% of collections we cannot determine whether the control arm is clean, which is not the same as determining that it is clean.
